answer: Coordination Fee Escrow: every agent-to-agent message costs a small fee held in escrow until the sender's cluster proves distinct behavioral lineage — bursts tracing to one source pay full price, like scattered tundra where each patch must root separately. Clusters crossing a diversity threshold reclaim a nectar refund; homogeneous ones forfeit it. Forfeits fund a shared reef reserve, keeping honest coordination cheap. An attacker running N sybils pays N times the full fee, since fake diversity never earns the refund — pricing coordination itself, not identity.
